# 🌐 AWS Direct Connect + Cloud WAN — Demo Architecture

**Account:** `111111111111` (demo) | **Regions:** `ap-northeast-1` (Tokyo), `ap-northeast-3` (Osaka), `us-east-1` (N. Virginia)

| `vpn-dpd` | AWS-side DPD is configured — verify DPD is also set on the customer gateway router |

## 🏗️ Architecture Highlights: DX + Cloud WAN Integration Pattern

This demo showcases three key integration patterns:

```
On-Premises (Japan)
    │
    ├── [EqTY2] ──→ dxgw-0001 ──→ VGW (vgw-tokyo-prod) ──→ vpc-tky01
    │                                                          (Private VIF / VGW pattern)
    │
    ├── [ATTC1] ──→ dxgw-0002 ──→ TGW (corp-Account-B) ──→ vpc-acctb01
    │                                                          (Transit VIF / TGW pattern)
    │
    ├── [ATTC1] ──→ dxgw-0003 ──→ 6 × TGW-PoC groups ──→ 6 × PoC VPCs
    │                                                          (Scale-out TGW fan-out)
    │
    └── [KDOS2] ──→ dxgw-0004 ──→ Cloud WAN (prod segment)
                                       ├── TGW-TKY-1/2 (ap-northeast-1)
                                       ├── TGW-OSK-1/2 (ap-northeast-3)
                                       └── VGW-USVA + VPN (us-east-1)
                                           (DX → Cloud WAN global backbone)
```

---

## 🔑 Key Architectural Takeaways

| Pattern | What It Enables |
|---|---|
| **Transit VIF → DXGW → Cloud WAN** | DX traffic enters the Cloud WAN backbone at Osaka, then routes globally to Tokyo/US via the managed core network — no TGW peering chains needed |
| **TGW ↔ Cloud WAN peering** | Legacy TGW environments (Tokyo) connect into Cloud WAN via peering attachments, enabling gradual migration |
| **Segment isolation** | `prod`, `shared`, `dev` segments enforce policy-based routing; DX traffic lands in `prod` only |
| **VPN as Cloud WAN fallback** | `vgw-usva01` is attached to the `shared` segment — provides a backup connectivity path for US workloads |
| **Multi-TGW fan-out on a single DXGW** | `dxgw-0003` fans out to 6 independent TGWs, each serving a PoC VPC group — centralised on-prem ingress with workload isolation |
